speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain along with difficulty wearing earrings. To understand what is happening, can you tell me exactly when this pain started and if it radiates to your jaw or teeth?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient is a 25-year-old female with a history of chronic bilateral ear infections and a right ear tympanoplasty performed 12 weeks ago, who now reports shooting ear pain when eating and difficulty wearing earrings. Given the history of ear infections and the specific nature of the pain triggered by chewing, does the pain also occur when you swallow or open your mouth wide?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myofascial Pain Syndrome involving the Ear (specifically Trigeminal Neuralgia or referred pain from TMJ dysfunction)

I must clarify that the previous suggestion of Tuberculosis is inconsistent with your symptoms of pain triggered by chewing and earring pressure; TB does not present this way. Since you mentioned pain when eating, does opening your mouth wide or touching your jaw trigger the shooting pain as well?
